name: Burger Söhne
desc: Fifth-generation Swiss family cigar group owning Dannemann (Germany) and Fabbrica Tabacchi Brissago, with brands such as Moods and Al Capone.
fit_rationale: Family cigar group with German and Swiss brands; no current scale figure found.
compliance: Tobacco company. EU Tobacco Advertising Directive 2003/33/EC bans tobacco sponsorship of events with cross-border effect and most tobacco advertising; WHO FCTC Art. 13 requires comprehensive advertising, promotion and sponsorship bans in ratifying states; national laws (e.g. German Tabakerzeugnisgesetz) add further limits. Any F1 deal would need legal review and could only cover non-tobacco branding, corporate hospitality or markets where permitted. Switzerland is outside the EU; Swiss Tobacco Products Act (in force 2024) restricts sponsorship of international events in Switzerland.
outstanding: Revenue and current employees (only 1965 figure on page).

name: Swisher International
desc: Jacksonville cigar and smokeless tobacco maker (Swisher Sweets, Drew Estate, Helme) shipping over two billion cigars a year to 70+ countries.
stores_or_sites: Plants in Jacksonville, Wheeling (WV) and Santiago (DR)
fit_rationale: Scale is evident (2bn cigars, 70+ countries) and its new caffeine pouches are non-tobacco, but current ownership is not confirmed on the page.
compliance: US tobacco company: FDA/Master Settlement Agreement limits on brand-name sponsorship for cigarettes and smokeless; EU sponsorship ban for cross-border events. Non-tobacco Mojo caffeine pouches would need separate legal review.
outstanding: Confirm private status (page lists it as privately held but does not confirm current owner); revenue.

name: Westons Cider
desc: Fourth-generation family-owned Herefordshire cider maker of Henry Westons, Stowford Press and Old Rosie, sold in over 44 countries.
fit_rationale: Family cider brand in 44 countries; Silverstone consumer activation possible but no scale figure found.
compliance: Alcohol company: alcohol advertising and sponsorship rules vary by market (France Loi Evin; restrictions in several Gulf and Asian GP hosts); F1 alcohol partners run responsible-drinking messaging.
